articles.title: Armenia's selective prosecution: A threat to EU relations?
articles.summary: While Brussels has refrained from harsh criticism, Armenian civil society has warned of selective justice against opposition figures. Could the EU's pragmatic stance risk repeating past mistakes?

image.caption: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan's government has positioned Armenia as an increasingly close partner of the European Union in the South CaucasusImage: Anthony Pizzoferrato/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: In early October, Artur Danielyan, leader of Armenia's opposition party Adekvad, was arrested following a Facebook post criticizing Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan.
The incident is part of a growing trend: Over the past two years, Armenian authorities have brought charges against multiple opposition figures, largely based on their social media activity.
Civil society representatives warn that such selective justice signals a worrying turn toward democratic backsliding.
The arrest of Artur Danielyan
The grounds for Danielyan's detention were Facebook posts in which he criticized both Pashinyan and the country's security services.

One point of contention was Pashinyan's stance on a possible prisoner exchange involving an Azerbaijani soldier accused of breaking into the home of a 39-year-old woman in the Armenian village of Shaki and injuring her and her children.

In an interview with Armenian news outlet Infocom, Pashinyan ruled out swapping the soldier imprisoned in Armenia for detained Armenians in Azerbaijan. Danielyan responded with a scathing attack, calling the prime minister a "scumbag" and accusing him of being unwilling to bring his fellow citizens home.

Armenia and Azerbaijan were in conflict for three decades over Nagorno-Karabakh, a breakaway Azerbaijani region populated by Armenians that declared independence in the 1990s. After Azerbaijan's military offensive in 2023, Baku regained control over the territory, forcing over 100,000 Armenians to flee. Currently, 19 Armenian individuals are being detained in Baku, including former high-ranking officials from Nagorno-Karabakh's de facto administration.

blocks.caption: Artur Danielyan, leader of the far-right "Adekvat" party, is a controversial figure in ArmeniaImage: Alexander Ryumin/TASS/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Growing trend of selective prosecutions?
Over a dozen Armenian civil society organizations have condemned the prosecution of the Adekvad party leader, calling it "patently illegal, disproportionate, and politically motivated."
"It is punitive in nature and sends a direct signal to the broader public aimed at silencing dissent, critical views, and undesirable speech", said the joint statement.
Several other criminal proceedings have been launched against activists who criticized the ruling establishment or Pashinyan.

Another prominent case emerged ahead of the parliamentary elections in June. Artur Osipyan, a displaced activist from Nagorno-Karabakh, was arrested after a verbal clash with Pashinyan over his Nagorno-Karabakh policy.

Following the incident, Armenian prosecutors indicted Osipyan for disrupting public order and obstructing the ruling party's campaign. He was also charged with inciting violence against Pashinyan in a social media post from March.
Is freedom of expression in danger in Armenia?
On April 15, 2020, Article 226.2 was added to the Criminal Code of Armenia, penalizing public calls to violence, as well as the public justification or promotion of violence.

After strong outrage by civil society, these offences were subsequently decriminalized. According to a 2025 report by Freedom House, "nearly 95% of court cases concerning incitement to violence under a 2020 criminal code amendment had involved alleged threats against Prime Minister Pashinyan and his supporters, whereas potentially prohibited statements by ruling party members were apparently not subject to the same scrutiny."

Throughout the 2026 pre-election period, the Regional Center for Democracy and Security (RCDS), an independent think tank based in Yerevan, monitored online hate speech targeting Nagorno-Karabakh refugees.

Their reports documented how pro-government bloggers and influential social media users used their platforms to direct hostile rhetoric toward displaced Karabakh Armenians, labeling them with derogatory terms. Despite these findings, law enforcement agencies in Armenia largely refrained from pursuing criminal prosecutions against these activists.
Why doesn't the EU react?
Despite Armenia's efforts to strengthen its ties with the EU, Brussels has given no clear response to the silencing of opposition voices, observers in Yerevan told DW.
"The EU, by and large, has adopted a very pragmatic and geopolitically driven approach," said political analyst Tigran Grigoryan.

"Given various regional developments, including what is happening in Georgia, Armenia has now become the EU's primary partner in the region," he added. "Coupled with the fact that the alternative to Pashinyan is a pro-Russian opposition, there is ultimately no serious response to these criminal cases."

Stefan Meister, Eastern Europe expert at the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP), echoed this view. European support for Armenia appears to be "mainly driven by the European Russia policy," Meister said. "So it's not so much about Armenia itself, but it is more about strengthening those forces that are undermining Russia's influence in the country and in the region."

He believes that Pashinyan leverages this geopolitical dynamic to label internal political opponents as Russian proxies. However, not everyone who criticizes Pashinyan is pro-Russian, Meister added. He pointed out that "the EU is somehow falling into this trap by accepting that this is the right narrative."
EU: Armenia should deliver on its commitment

Democracy, the rule of law, and fundamental rights are at the core of the EU-Armenia Comprehensive and Enhanced Partnership Agreement (CEPA) and the Strategic Agenda for the EU-Armenia Partnership, an EU spokesperson said in a written response to DW's request for comment.

It also pointed out that "the EU is closely following developments in the country, including as regards criminal investigations. In line with Armenia's international commitments and legal framework, such investigations should be carried out in an independent and impartial manner, free from political considerations."

articles.title: What we know about Krakow mass shooting so far
articles.summary: At least six people were killed by a gunman in military fatigues who opened fire in Poland's second largest city.

blocks.text: Image source, Agencja Wyborcza.pl/Reuters
ByFlorence Freeman and Emer Moreau

At least six people have been killed and several others injured after a gunman opened fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland. Details are still emerging - here is everything we know so far.
How did the attack unfold?
The attack began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's Main Market Square, the bustling central point of the city.
Police said a man drove into the square before beginning to fire "at random people from his car".
Footage from the scene shows scenes of panic as people fled, with the sound of gunfire clearly heard.

items: Follow live updates from Krakow

blocks.text: People run for shelter as gunshots heard in Krakow
Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the attacker.
The gunman was shot but is alive and has been arrested.
Distressing footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows the moment a police officer confronts the suspect on the ground before firing his weapon several times.
The officer then falls to the ground, apparently having been injured himself.
Moment police officer appears to shoot Krakow suspect
Shop windows in the square have signs of damage, seemingly from bullets, with glass shards scattered along the floor.
City officials have urged people who live in the city and tourists to stay away from the area while an investigation continues.
How many people have died and been injured?
Six people - four women and two men - are confirmed to have been killed.
At least 15 people have been injured, including two police officers who were shot while detaining the attacker.

One of the police officers was described as being in a "very critical condition" by a Polish government minister after being shot three times while arresting the attacker. The officer is undergoing surgery, he added.
Polish authorities have not confirmed the names and ages of the other victims.

blocks.caption: A map showing Krakow Main Square Market

blocks.text: What do we know about the suspect and motive?
Police have confirmed the attacker was a male Polish citizen but no further details about his identity have been released.
The suspect was wearing "military-style attire" and had a military-grade weapon, according to a police spokesperson
"Many pieces of weapons and ammunition were found in his vehicle", the spokesperson added.
Nothing has been publicly confirmed about the motive behind the attack so far.
How did witnesses describe the attack?
The shooting happened in one of the largest medieval squares in Europe, a busy location which is also a popular tourist destination.
Jonathan Balshaw from Ipswich was there with his Polish girlfriend Dominika. The couple were outside St Mary's Basilica, in the corner of the square, when the shooting started.
Jonathan said: "We ran down the side of the church and through the side door and hid with several other people until the gunfire died down.
"A lot of shots were fired, more than 20 with it sounding like multiple different firearms - there were two distinctly different noises."
Caitlin Shasby from Newcastle arrived in Krakow yesterday with her friend Jon for a long weekend.
She said they heard shots from their hotel room but were not sure what was happening until their hotel rang them and told them to "stay in our rooms until further notice".
Moment shooting heard in Krakow square
What has the reaction been in Poland and internationally?
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk is on his way to Krakow and is expected to give an address later on Saturday.
Earlier, he said he was being kept informed by the interior minister and that police were investigating "the background and all the circumstances".
President Karol Nawrocki said he was "deeply concerned" and was awaiting "a full explanation of the circumstances surrounding these tragic events".
US ambassador to Poland Tom Rose described it as a "savage and murderous attack".
The EU's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said the shooting was "a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland".

articles.title: US offers $20m reward for information about Iran's nuclear programme
articles.summary: Donald Trump has repeatedly raised the prospecting of renewing strikes against Iran's nuclear facilities.

blocks.text: A US State Department statement about its multi-million dollar reward said it was offering the money for information about the Iranian programme, including "facilities, equipment and associated personnel".

It said Iran's "lack of compliance with the IAEA [the International Atomic Energy Agency] on safeguards obligations has led to the agency's loss of 'continuity of knowledge' regarding Iran's production and inventory of key components like [nuclear] centrifuges".
Centrifuges are needed to produce enriched uranium, which can be used to make reactor fuel for civilian use but also for nuclear weapons if enriched to around 90% purity or higher.

There had been mounting speculation that the US might resume significant strikes in Iran after the midterm elections, though Trump told reporters, prior to the polls, that he was in "no rush" to do so.
In an interview with Fox News on the eve of the midterms, the president also said the US "might need to go after Pickaxe [Mountain]", an underground site linked to Iran's nuclear programme.
This was "not a big deal" and could be done in "one hour", Trump said.
The president has repeatedly threatened to bomb the suspected underground site on previous occasions.

However, both Trump and Vice-President JD Vance have said public opposition to the war on Iran fuelled heavy losses for their Republican Party in this week's midterm elections, which has led to speculation the White House may no longer seek an escalation in the conflict.
On Friday, Trump insisted that Iran was keen to end the eight-month conflict with the US, stressing the damage to Tehran's economy and military.
"We're dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly," he said.
Qatar's foreign ministry spokesman said on Tuesday that both sides were "reviewing the ideas and proposals we have presented" and that it remained hopeful of a deal being agreed.
Iranian negotiators had discussed with mediators a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days once the US met its seven conditions.

The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.

articles.title: South Africa's ANC facing worst-ever performance in local elections
articles.summary: Near-final results show South Africa's once dominant ANC will see its lowest-ever vote percentage. The party is taking the blame for shoddy municipal services, including water and electricity…

image.caption: Millions of South Africans headed to the polls across the country's municipalities to elect local councilors and mayors (Photo: November 4)Image: Leandre Steenberg/Matrix Images/picture alliance

blocks.text: South Africa's African National Congress (ANC) is heading for an historically poor election performance, with the near-final tally from Wednesday's municipal polls showing it coming in with just over 30% of the vote.
The ANC also lost its majority in six of the eight metropolitan regions, South Africa's Electoral Commission said Saturday in sharing the results after 98% of votes were counted.

South African voters in 2026 are angry about water and electricity shortages, with the ANC taking the blame for the poor state of municipalities. High unemployment, crime, and widespread corruption are other pressing issues.

ANC leader, and South African president, Cyril Ramaphosa, has not yet addressed the poor performance as of Saturday evening. However, during the week, he admitted in his weekly presidential letter that "municipal failures have contributed to declining public trust and confidence in democratic governance."
On Saturday, ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula told reporters that the ANC needs to work on winning back public confidence.
"We cannot ask the people to trust us merely because of our history," Mbalula said.
"This has been a very catastrophic outcome for the ANC ... as much as we are the largest party, it has been catastrophic for the movement," he added.
The ANC's steady decline with voters

Although the ANC will still be the single largest party by overall vote percentage, it had governed with an absolute majority for most of its history up until the general election in 2024 saw it lose an outright parliamentary majority for the first time in South Africa's democratic era.
"This is the most severe result that the ANC would have feared," political analyst Daniel Silke told the AFP news agency.

"It's the ANC's worst result in history," Silke said, adding that the result will undermine the ANC's ability to exert authority on the local and national level. The results could also provide a bellwether of voter sentiment ahead of the 2029 general elections.
Once led by Nelson Mandela, the ANC was instrumental in ending apartheid, and took and power in 1994 after South Africa became a democracy.

But over the past decade, it has steadily performed worse in one election after another. In 2024, the ANC secured just over 40% in the 2024 national polls and 46% at the previous municipal elections in 2021.
After losing the absolute majority in 2024, the ANC formed a cross-party national unity government with all the parties represented in parliament, which is still in power.

The ANC's decline comes amid disillusionment over corruption, mismanagement and high unemployment. Smaller parties have also emerged across South Africa's political landscape, cutting into the ANC's voter base.
DA opposition holds large cities
South Africa is now looking at complex coalition negotiations for municipal level governing alliances.
Runner up in the polls looks to be the pro-business, center-right Democratic Alliance (DA), coming in at 24% of the votes.

The DA is set to keep control of Cape Town after winning an absolute majority. It also performed well in the capital, Pretoria, and economic hub of Johannesburg, and is expected to form coalitions that exclude the ANC.

"All of the cut and thrust that comes with the election is now over, and it is time now... to put together governments that can actually fix these towns and cities," DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis told reporters.
"We have already reached out to many parties over the last 24 hours and will continue to do so today," he said.

articles.title: LTO summons bus driver, operator after engine cover kills pedestrian in Quezon
articles.summary: The Land Transportation Office (LTO) has issued a show-cause order (SCO) against the driver and operator of a passenger bus involved in the death of a pedestrian in Atimonan, Quezon.

blocks.text: Published November 8, 2026 2:05am
The Land Transportation Office (LTO) has issued a show-cause order (SCO) against the driver and operator of a passenger bus involved in the death of a pedestrian in Atimonan, Quezon.
The incident occurred at around 5 a.m. on November 5, 2026, along the northbound lane of Maharlika Highway in Barangay Tagbakin, the LTO said in a news release.

According to a police report, the bus was traversing the highway when its engine cover suddenly detached while the vehicle was moving and hit a pedestrian standing by the roadside while waiting for a ride to Manila.
The victim sustained serious injuries and was rushed to Doña Marta Hospital. The victim was declared dead on arrival.
The LTO identified the bus driver and operator and formally served them with the SCO, according to LTO chief Assistant Secretary Markus Lacanilao

Under the order, the driver and operator are required to appear before the LTO Central Office's Intelligence and Investigation Division (IID) on November 13 to submit their sworn statements and explanations, along with supporting documents, regarding the alleged violation of reckless driving.
The bus operator is also facing charges of employing a reckless driver and breach of franchise conditions.
The LTO said the driver's license may be suspended or revoked if the agency's final decision finds him to be an improper person to operate a motor vehicle.
As part of its immediate action, the agency ordered the driver to surrender his license to the IID for a 90-day suspension. The bus has also been placed under alarm.

"Negligence in maintaining a passenger bus in good condition should never result in the loss of life. Every part and component of a vehicle must be ensured to be safe and in proper working condition before it travels, as even a single oversight can lead to a road tragedy," Lacanilao said.
The LTO assured the public that those found violating transportation laws and regulations would be held accountable.
It also vowed to intensify its monitoring of the roadworthiness of public utility vehicles to prevent similar incidents and protect the lives of all road users. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Gaza wedding festival sees 250 couples married at the same time
articles.summary: A mass wedding for Palestinian brides and grooms has taken place in the rubble-strewn streets of Gaza.

blocks.text: Amid the ruins of destroyed buildings and displaced people's tents, Gazans gathered to celebrate a mass wedding for Palestinian brides and grooms.

The ceremony, organised by the UAE's humanitarian mission Operation Gallant Knight 3, brought together brides and grooms from across Gaza for a celebration of what organisers described as love and new beginnings in the besieged enclave.
There has been a ceasefire in Gaza since last October, but it is fragile.
The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.
Israel responded by launching a military campaign against Hamas in Gaza, during which more than 74,640 people have been killed, according to the territory's health ministry.

articles.title: Six dead after gunman opens fire ‘at random’ in Kraków market square
articles.summary: Reports say man fired shots from from his car in Poland’s second city before being wounded by police while trying to flee

blocks.text: Six people have been killed and 15 injured after a shooting in a market square in Kraków, Poland.
A man who had driven into the square at about 3pm began “firing at random people from his car”, according to a statement by local police on X.
The gunman was a Polish citizen who acted alone and was shot and wounded during a gunfight with police nearby, authorities said.
He used a long military-type firearm, the police said.
Police officers are among the wounded.

blocks.caption: Five killed in Krakow market square shooting

blocks.text: The incident took place in the main market square, a popular tourist destination in Kraków, Poland’s second-largest city.

A tram driver reported about 3pm that his vehicle was shot at from a man in a moving car while passing nearby the main square, the Krakow municipal transport company said. The window to the tram driver’s cabin was shattered.
The prime minister, Donald Tusk, confirmed the shooting after initial reports by local media, which cited police and the fire department.

“I am being kept informed by the minister of the interior about the situation in Kraków following the tragic shooting,” he wrote on X, adding that “the police are investigating the background and all the circumstances of the attack”.
Later in the evening, government spokesperson Adam Szlapka wrote on X: “Today’s event in Kraków has shaken all of Poland,” adding that “Prime minister Donald Tusk is on his way to Kraków”
after newsletter promotion
The justice minister, Waldemar Żurek, wrote on X that authorities would “ensure that the perpetrator of this crime is held fully accountable and severely punished”.
The Polish president, Karol Nawrocki, said he was “deeply concerned by reports of the tragic events” in Kraków, and that his thoughts are with victims, those injured and their families.
An interior minister is heading to the scene, according to reports.
Earlier this year, Euronews reported that the number of legally owned firearms in Poland surpassed 1 million for the first time.

Poland issued a record 50,700 gun permits in 2025, and the number of active permits registered in 2025 was almost double the number registered in 2015, according to the police statistics cited in the report.

articles.title: Houthis say at least 25 killed in Saudi air strike
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia, which leads a coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen, has not commented.

blocks.text: Media linked to the Houthi movement in Yemen say that at least 25 people, including women and children, have been killed in airstrikes by Saudi Arabia.
There has been no comment from the Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government in Yemen.

Live video footage on Al Masirah - a television station run by the Houthis - has shown rescuers pulling bodies out of the rubble of several buildings in al-Shariyah, a town to the east of the capital, Sanaa.
The bodies of young children can be seen among those dug out from the ruins.
The television station has also shown a number of injured people being carried on stretchers to hospital.
Saba news agency, which is also run by the Houthis, said the attack was carried out by Saudi Arabia.
The Saudis have led a coalition that has been fighting the Houthis for more than a decade in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government.
The war in Yemen had been dormant for several years but reignited as a result of the Iran war.
A truce began to fall apart when Saudi Arabia struck the airport in Sanaa - which is controlled by the Houthis - to prevent an Iranian plan landing there.

The Tehran-backed Houthis subsequently targeted Abha airport in Saudi Arabia, then began hitting Saudi ships that have been using the Red Sea off the coast of Yemen as an alternative oil export route to the Strait of Hormuz.
Major fighting has since resumed in Yemen between the Houthis and forces fighting for the Saudi-backed government of Yemen.
On Friday, an attack on a market in Taiz province, which has been the focus of much of the recent fighting, is reported to have killed 30 people.
The Houthis accused the Saudis of carrying out the strike, while government forces accused the Houthis of having fired a missile at the site.
The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed.
The Saudis have regularly bombed Houthi positions, while the group has fired multiple missiles at targets inside Saudi Arabia, including airports and oil facilities.
Hours before the strike that hit al-Shariyah, the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a missile heading towards Riyadh.
A Houthi leader, Mahdi al-Mashat, has vowed that the group will take revenge for the latest attacks in Yemen.

articles.title: Italian foreign minister says hackers leaked his personal data
articles.summary: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has blamed pro-Russian hackers for publishing the details online.

blocks.text: Italy's Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani says he has been targeted by "cyber-criminals" who published his personal data online because of his country's support for Ukraine.
"For days now, cyber-criminals have been publishing my personal data on the dark web and seeking further information, effectively exposing me to new threats and intimidation," Tajani wrote on X.
He did not specify the nature of the threats, but said the hackers were also targeting his family.
The dark web is a hidden part of the internet that is not indexed by common search engines and can only be accessed with specialist software.
"Our position on Ukraine is the political reason I have been targeted," Tajani said.
"Defending the freedom of a sovereign state, taking a clear stand in support of a nation's democracy and independence, is dangerous in the eyes of these criminal entities."
Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni blamed the incident on pro-Russian hackers and offered Tajani her "full solidarity".
"The sale of confidential information about institutional representatives is a cause of serious concern and must be tackled with the utmost determination," she said in a statement.
Moscow has not publicly responded to the allegations.
Meloni also expressed concern about "circulation of false images" which she said were shared by members of Italy's opposition. She did not give details about the content of the images.
The Italian government has provided humanitarian and military support to Ukraine in its war against Russia.
Tajani, who is also the deputy prime minister, said the government was taking the threats seriously.

articles.title: More than 40,000 gather as Pope Leo XIV celebrates Mass in Uruguay
articles.summary: Massive crowds have turned out for the pontiff as he celebrates the first Mass of his South America tour. A nighttime prayer vigil in Montevideo is expected to draw more than 60,000 young people.

image.caption: Tens of thousands have been turning out to hear Pope Leo XIV's message of Christian charity and brotherly love, as on Saturday in Uruguay Image: Tiziana Fabi/AFP

blocks.text: The Vatican and local authorities in western Uruguay say an estimated 40,000 people turned out on Saturday morning to participate in the first Mass of Pope Leo XIV's 12-day, three-nation tour of South America.

The Vatican said 30,000 people from Uruguay as well as neighboring Argentina and Brazil had registered for the event, adding that another 10,000 had braved the rain to attend the religious service, which took place in Paysandu — a city on the Uruguay River, some 375 kilometers (230 miles) west of the capital Montevideo.
Leo, who underwent surgery for lung cancer on October 13, was greeted by throngs of cheering fans as he made his way from the local airport to Paysandu's sprawling Paris London Park.
"He's the representative of Christ but he's human," said Soledad Sanchez, who told France's AFP news agency that she had traveled far to be in Paysandu.

"We weren't sure if he could make it but he pushed through for us," said Sanchez as tears welled up in her eyes, "He made it here to give us a message of peace because he knows our world needs it right now."
What to know about Pope Leo XIV's lung cancer
Why are young people reacting so strongly to Pope Leo XIV?

The 71-year-old US-born pontiff, who holds US, Peruvian and Vatican citizenship, is seeking to raise interest in the Catholic Church in Uruguay, South America's most secular country, as a remedy for helping the nation and its citizens cope with the troubles of the modern world.
Saturday morning's Mass was dedicated to the Blessed Jacinto Vera, who was appointed Uruguay's first bishop by Pope Leo XIII in 1878.

On Friday, the leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics spoke of Bishop Vera, noting that he had walked the countryside and helped the poor, adding that those whom he encountered "found something of Christ's goodness" in him.

Leo will underscore the need for that kind of outreach on Saturday afternoon when he visits a Montevideo neighborhood beset by drug violence and in which the Church has invested in public housing and rehabilitation projects for addicts.

At Pope Leo's final event in the country — a prayer vigil in Montevideo's Centenary Stadium that is expected to draw some 60,000 young faithful — the pontiff will call on young people to reject religious indifference and turn to Christ's teachings.
Leo's emphasis on charity and brotherly love has struck a deep chord with young people in Uruguay and elsewhere.

One 18-year-old attendee at Saturday morning's Mass told AFP: "I wouldn't call myself religious, but I like this pope. He has a really good message for humanity. Even for non-believers, there is something to take from his ideas."

On Sunday, Pope Leo will depart for Argentina, where he will meet with President Javier Milei, a libertarian-populist and close ally to US President Donald Trump, who previously lashed out at the leader of the world's largest Christian faith over his calls to end wars and cruel immigration policies.

articles.title: DBM: P82.9B set for government workers' bonuses, cash gifts
articles.summary: The government will spend P82.9 billion on bonuses and cash gifts for public sector employees, the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) said Saturday, as it reminded agencies to ensure the…

blocks.text: Published November 8, 2026 12:21am

The government will spend P82.9 billion on bonuses and cash gifts for public sector employees, the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) said Saturday, as it reminded agencies to ensure the timely release of the benefits.
Under DBM Budget Circular No. 2024-3, qualified government employees are entitled to a year-end bonus equivalent to one month’s basic pay as of October 31, 2026.
State employees will also receive a P5,000 cash gift.
The DBM said that of the P82.998 billion, P73.449 billion is intended for the bonus and P9.549 billion is for the cash gift.

“Ang Year-End Bonus po ng mga government employees na katumbas ng one month basic salary, kasama ang P5,000 Cash Gift, ay dapat matanggap kasabay ng first salary for November. Na-release na po ng DBM ang pondo para rito, kaya we want to remind our agencies to ensure the timely release of these benefit,” DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon said in a statement.

(The Year-End Bonus of government employees is equivalent to one month's basic salary, including a P5,000 Cash Gift, which should be received with the first salary for November. The DBM has released the funds for this, so we want to remind agencies to ensure the timely release of these benefits.)

“Alam po natin na malaking tulong ito sa ating mga kawani at kanilang pamilya, especially ngayong papalapit na ang Pasko. More importantly, this is our way of recognizing and thanking our government workers for their hard work, dedication, and continued service to the Filipino people,” he added.

(We know that this is a big help for our workers and their families, especially now that Christmas is near. More importantly, this is our way of recognizing and thanking our government workers for their hard work, dedication, and continued service to the Filipino people.)

Government personnel must have rendered at least four months of aggregate service (120 days) from January 1 to October 31 to qualify for the full year-end bonus and cash gifts. The DBM said that qualifying service included actual service rendered in regular, contractual, or casual positions in both national and local government. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: NPC probing government data leaks
articles.summary: The National Privacy Commission is investigating reports of data leaks involving several government agencies.

blocks.text: November 8, 2026 | 12:00am
NPC Deputy Privacy Commissioner Jose Belarmino II said the commission is verifying the incidents and determining whether personal information has been compromised.
STAR / File
MANILA, Philippines — The National Privacy Commission (NPC) is investigating reports of data leaks involving several government agencies.

“The Commission will coordinate directly with the government agencies identified in these reports to verify the alleged incidents, ascertain the circumstances surrounding them and determine whether personal data have been compromised,” he said.
Belarmino said the concerned agencies must submit the necessary reports in compliance with Republic Act 10173, or the Data Privacy Act, if warranted.
The NPC has yet to receive personal data breach notifications from the concerned government institutions. Among the agencies reportedly affected by a data breach is the Bureau of Internal Revenue.
Under NPC Circular 16-03, personal information controllers are required to notify the commission and affected data subjects within 72 hours of learning that a data breach has occurred.
Should the reported incidents be confirmed and meet the requirements for mandatory notification, the concerned agencies must submit the prescribed breach notifications.
“The NPC will continue to monitor developments and take appropriate regulatory action, as warranted, to ensure the protection of personal data and uphold the rights of data subjects,” Belarmino said.
Fake account
Meanwhile, the Philippine National Police is investigating a fraudulent Facebook account using the photograph of PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr.
The PNP vowed yesterday to pursue appropriate action against those responsible for the unauthorized use of Nartatez’s name and photograph.
It warned the public against engaging with the account operating under the name Jose Melencio Corpus, stressing that it has no connection with the police chief.
Netizens were advised to exercise caution, particularly if the account requests money, personal information or favors.

“The PNP emphasizes that any messages, instructions, requests or transactions made through the said account are unauthorized and must not be treated as official PNP communications,” the PNP said in a statement.
Those who received messages from the bogus account were advised to take screenshots as evidence that could be used by the PNP Anti-Cybercrime Group in its investigation.
Fake news

In a separate case involving alleged online disinformation, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla said he would file complaints against vloggers and Facebook pages spreading false information about his health and his office to undermine public confidence.

During a press briefing on Nov. 6, Remulla said he would file complaints with the Department of Information and Communications Technology and Facebook, seeking the removal of accounts spreading false information for propaganda purposes.

“People are trying to create doubt about the office or maybe even the state of my health and I think this has to stop. Obviously, it’s meant to influence people so they will have doubts about this government and this office,” he said.

Remulla said he learned about the false reports concerning his health after media friends expressed concern and told him they were praying for him. He clarified that he had been cancer-free for three years. — Daphne Galvez

articles.title: Likhang Filipino Theatre in Pasay opens its doors
articles.summary: President Marcos and First Lady Liza Marcos on Friday inaugurated the 279-seat Likhang Filipino Theatre along Roxas Boulevard in Pasay, a new hub for artists to showcase their work and support the…

blocks.text: November 8, 2026 | 12:00am

President Marcos, accompanied by First Lady Liza Marcos and former first lady Imelda Marcos, lead the ribbon-cutting ceremony for the newly opened Likhang Filipino Theatre in Pasay on on November 6, 2026.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos and First Lady Liza Marcos on Friday inaugurated the 279-seat Likhang Filipino Theatre along Roxas Boulevard in Pasay, a new hub for artists to showcase their work and support the Philippines’ creative industry.

“With the opening of the Likhang Filipino Theatre, we now have another home for our artists and performers, where they can bring our stories to life and inspire a new generation of Filipino talent,” the Chief Executive said in a social media post yesterday.
“Filipino creativity has always been a source of great pride for our country. What our artists need are more opportunities to develop their talents and share their work with the world,” he added.
Marcos thanked his wife Liza for what he described as her “continued dedication” to Filipino artists and the creative community.

Likhang Filipino was formed last January to promote Filipino craftsmanship, design, innovation and creative enterprise and to link Filipino-made products with local and international markets. Managed by the trade department’s Center for International Trade Expositions and Missions, Likhang Filipino is the country’s year-round showroom, marketplace and incubation hub for locally-made products.

The theatre, which is designed to provide artists a platform for their work without the scale and production demands of a grand theatre, is a venue within the Likhang Filipino Creative Lab. The lab is an “open, shared space for Filipino creatives to learn, create and collaborate through co-working, training and creative facilities,” according to the Presidential Communications Office.

articles.title: Groups back DFA on sustained talks with China
articles.summary: A total of 20 labor, business and civil society organizations expressed support for the call of the Department of Foreign Affairs to sustain dialogue and cooperation with China, citing its importance…

blocks.text: November 8, 2026 | 12:00am
DFA Aseana.
Philstar.com / Irish Lising

MANILA, Philippines — A total of 20 labor, business and civil society organizations expressed support for the call of the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) to sustain dialogue and cooperation with China, citing its importance in advancing national interest and promoting economic growth.
In a joint statement yesterday, the groups welcomed DFA Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro’s recent engagement with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi.
Lazaro said both sides emphasized the need for continued diplomatic dialogue and mutual respect for differences.
The ministers’ discussion covered the state and direction of bilateral relations following a series of heated exchanges between the Chinese embassy in Manila and some Philippine officials.

“We recognize the DFA’s pragmatic and statesmanlike approach in protecting the country’s national interests, particularly its economic development, trade and exports, tourism, overseas Filipino workers and other vital bilateral engagements with China, the Philippines’ largest trading partner,” the groups said.

Amid global uncertainty and intensifying competition, the groups said other Southeast Asian countries are strengthening partnerships with China to promote trade, investment, technology, infrastructure and tourism.
For the groups, the Philippines should do the same by pursuing mutually beneficial economic opportunities through constructive engagement.
While the groups are pushing for continued engagement with China, they emphasized the need to continue to uphold the Philippines’ sovereignty and national interests.

“We therefore support the DFA’s pursuit of principled diplomacy and sustained dialogue over confrontation, recognizing that a balanced and constructive relationship with China is essential to advancing Philippine economic security, national interests and sustainable development,” the groups said.

The joint statement was issued by the Asian Association of Academic Administrators and Educators Inc., Employers Confederation of the Philippines, Federation of Filipino-Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry Inc., Federation of Free Workers, Federation of Philippine Industries Inc., Foreign Buyers Association of the Philippines, GS1 Philippines, OFW Foundation, Philippine Amalgamated Supermarkets Association, Philippine Association of Legitimate Service Contractors, Philippine Association of Salt Industry Networks Inc., Philippine Chamber of Agriculture and Food Inc., Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Philippine Exporters Confederation Inc., Philippine Food Processors and Exporters Organization Inc., Philippine Franchise Association, Philippine Retailers Association, Philippine Young Entrepreneurs Association, Semiconductor and Electronic Industries in the Philippines Foundation Inc. and Women’s Business Council Philippines.
Earlier, various groups also called for the de-escalation of tensions with China, citing risks to deep trade and economic ties if tensions persist.
China and Hong Kong serve as the Philippines’ largest trading partner, accounting for nearly 30 percent of the country’s total international trade in recent years.
China is also a source of remittances and tourists for the Philippines.

articles.title: DENR, CCC, UNDP to develop response framework on climate-related losses
articles.summary: The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) said it is working to advance a strategic and coordinated response to climate-related loss and damage.

blocks.text: Published November 7, 2026 11:32pm
The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) said it is working to advance a strategic and coordinated response to climate-related loss and damage.

The DENR is developing the national framework in partnership with the Climate Change Commission (CCC) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Philippines, according to a press release issued by the agency on Saturday.
DENR Secretary Atty. Juan Miguel Cuna said the initiative comes at a critical time, as Filipinos continue to face challenges from climate-related events.

“Every year, millions of Filipinos experience the impacts of extreme weather events, from homes damaged by typhoons and floods to livelihoods disrupted by droughts and changing weather patterns. While communities continue to adapt to climate change, many impacts can no longer be avoided, creating losses that affect lives, culture, health, livelihoods, and local economies,” Cuna said.

“Recognizing these growing challenges, the Philippines is developing a national Climate-related Loss and Damage Framework and Strategy that will guide how government, development partners, and other stakeholders work together to support communities affected by climate impacts. The strategy seeks to strengthen coordination, improve access to financing, enhance knowledge and data systems, and ensure that assistance reaches those most affected,” he added.

For this initiative, the government convened the first meeting of the Development Partners Coordination Group on Climate-related Loss and Damage (L&DDPCG), which is designed to align financing, technical assistance, and institutional support in line with the framework's priorities.

DENR said this mechanism will help strengthen coordination across development partners, reduce fragmentation, identify gaps and opportunities for collaboration, and mobilize resources for vulnerable communities.
During the meeting, the agency said participating agencies agreed to establish systems-focused workstreams to unite key government bodies and development partners in implementing the strategy.
“These workstreams will support policy development, financing solutions, local action, and institutional strengthening,” the DENR said.
According to the DENR, the key government agencies working alongside development partners to implement the framework are:

articles.title: UK cannot 'cherry pick' EU single market deal, Barnier tells BBC
articles.summary: The former Brexit negotiator says EU countries would reject any British attempts to follow economic rules "a la carte".

blocks.text: The EU's former Brexit negotiator has warned that the UK cannot "cherry pick" which elements of the single market to which it subscribes, after Andy Burnham said he wanted to explore closer economic ties with Europe.
The prime minister has said rejoining the bloc's internal market was among options he could pursue as part of a reshaping of ties since the UK's exit from the EU nearly six years ago.
But Michel Barnier told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that EU members would insist on the UK readopting certain conditions, such as the free movement of people, to gain access.
He said there was not a "single market à la carte" menu from which the UK could pick and choose what elements it wanted to adopt.

Barnier - who led the EU delegation during Brexit talks between 2016 and 2021, and had a three-month spell as French prime minister in 2024 - said the "door is open" within Europe to the UK rejoining as an EU member.
But he insisted that any move to rejoin the single market - which allows for goods to be freely traded without border controls - would require the UK to follow the same terms as other members.

He added that this included compliance with regulations designed to promote the circulation of goods, services, capital and people, referred to collectively within EU institutions as the "four freedoms".
"There will be no possibility to have one freedom and not the other. The four freedoms are clearly the four conditions to be inside a single market."

Since becoming prime minister in July, Burnham has suggested he could commit Labour to pursuing a much closer future relationship with Europe, including asking to rejoin the organisation as a full member, though he has ruled out major changes before the next election.
His predecessors have struck a series of deals with the EU on different aspects of how the UK and EU interact post-Brexit.
Both sides are hoping to use a meeting in Brussels in 10 days' time to unveil deals on food standards, youth visas and re-linking British industry to the EU's carbon trading regime.
Of the four freedoms, the free movement of people - which allows EU citizens to live and work elsewhere in the bloc without a visa - was a key issue during the 2016 Brexit referendum.

Burnham's immediate predecessor, Sir Keir Starmer, ruled out re-establishing it for the UK in Labour's 2024 election manifesto and any move to advocate it again would prove a key dividing line with the Conservatives and Reform UK at a future poll.

Burnham recently said in an interview that he would not re-establish free movement of people without a referendum, prompting Downing Street to clarify that he was not advocating its return at this point.

He has previously said he wanted to lay out "different options" for the relationship with Europe at the Brussels summit later this month, before trying to find a consensus with the British public on a new relationship.

Barnier also predicted that EU countries would reject reinstating the British financial rebate, first negotiated in 1985, that lowered UK contributions towards the EU's annual budget while it was a member.
The UK's decision to leave the bloc had created "a new situation", he said, meaning a new rebate would be "off the table".
Barnier also compared Reform leader Nigel Farage to French politician Marine Le Pen. He said: "We have our own Farage. It is Mrs Le Pen. The same populism, the same lies, the same false promises."

Asked by Kuenssberg to clarify what he was referring to with his accusation of lies, Barnier said "for instance, when Mr Farage and Mr Johnson promised the UK people to get back [£350] million per week, it was not true, it was not possible. It was a lie".

The Vote Leave campaign, of which Boris Johnson became a key figure, has been criticised previously for the slogan on the side of their campaign bus that said Britain sent £350m a week to the EU, adding: "Let's fund our NHS instead".

Johnson said in 2017 that "once we have settled our accounts, we will take back control of roughly £350m per week. It would be a fine thing as many of us have pointed out if a lot of that money went on the NHS".
Critics have said that the £350m per week was an approximate sum which represents a "gross contribution" and did not take into account the UK's £75m-a-week rebate nor the EU's investments in the UK.
Johnson has since defended the claim, saying the £350m was based on the UK's gross contribution to the EU, and was in fact an underestimate as UK contributions were due to rise.

​In his memoirs published in 2024, Johnson said EU money spent in the UK was not "democratically controlled by the British people", and "even if the net figure was only £175m, that was still a hell of a lot of money".

Farage, who led Leave UK and was not part of the Vote Leave campaign so not connected to the £350m claim, said: "It is the same old Barnier - arrogant, out of touch and a bully. He vindicates our decision to leave every time he opens his mouth."

articles.title: Rodrigo Duterte defense challenges expert report bid
articles.summary: PRAGUE, Czech Republic - Among the expert reports that International Criminal Court (ICC) prosecutors are seeking to admit as evidence, former President Rodrigo Duterte"s defense is challenging one…
articles.byline: ANDY PEÑAFUERTE III, JAY-VEE MARASIGAN PANGAN

blocks.text: PRAGUE, Czech Republic – Among the expert reports that International Criminal Court (ICC) prosecutors are seeking to admit as evidence, former President Rodrigo Duterte’s defense is challenging one that cites external materials not considered an “integral part” of a witness’s evidence.

In a publicly redacted request released on November 6, Duterte’s counsel, Peter Haynes, opposed introducing and using two external studies as associated materials for P-1400’s Expert Report, calling it an “improper attempt” by the Office of Prosecution (OTP).

It may be recalled that on October 23, prosecutors informed Trial Chamber III that P-1400 – an expert in a currently undisclosed field – provided the Expert Report covering redacted topics relevant to Duterte’s ICC case.
Aside from this document, the prosecution requested to admit 15 associated items in its fourth application under Rule 68(3).
In his response, Haynes said that the defense does not object in principle to introducing P-1400’s Expert Report via Rule 68(3), rather than full viva voce testimony.
However, he argued that the expert report “contains [REDACTED] footnotes citing other sources, [REDACTED] of which the Prosecution now seeks to introduce.”

Haynes noted that P-1400 “has not meaningfully used or explained” the two studies in question and that they “are not integral” but “merely reproduce information already provided in” the witness’s report.
“Their introduction would be redundant, and would burden the Chamber with evidence of negligible relevance, contrary to its express directions.”
In the filing, Haynes stated that a redacted individual or entity contributed to the first study, whose “treatment of the considerably wider findings of this item is extremely limited.”
He also mentioned another study – whose topic and preparer remain concealed – that contains “contextual information that does not form part of the P-1400’s own inquiry.”

“In reality, the Prosecution is attempting indirectly to introduce material prepared by other professionals who are not on its witness list via the instant Expert Report which – by its own admission – only “[REDACTED],” Haynes argued.

During the final status conference on November 2, Haynes described P-1400’s expert report as “difficult” and told Presiding Judge Joanna Korner that the defense would need “a couple of hours” to cross-examine.
In the filing, Haynes noted that there would be “merit” in hearing a redacted testimony “concurrently with that of the Defence expert”.

Additionally, he asked Trial Chamber III to either dismiss the OTP’s application for P-1400 or consider this request from the defense in a pending decision on the prosecution’s prior request to add the documents to its List of Evidence after the deadline.
Some witnesses may testify remotely
In a separate filing also dated November 6, prosecutors submitted an updated list of witnesses ahead of Duterte’s trial.

Trial Chamber III had ordered prosecutors to identify witnesses expected to testify through audio-video link, or AVL, and provide their expected order of appearance and any foreseeable problems with remote testimony.

At the November 2 status conference, senior trial lawyer Julian Nicholls told Korner that about 29 witnesses would participate via an audio-video link, and that the number could be broken down into categories.
In the latest filing, the prosecution said it has now marked in its confidential list the witnesses who may testify via AVL and updated their anticipated calling order.
The public filing does not disclose the number or identities of the witnesses because the updated list is in a confidential annex.
Prosecutors said they would inform the Chamber if circumstances later allow these witnesses to appear in person.
At present, the prosecutors said they do not foresee any issues with testimony through an audio-video link.
During the status conference, Director of the ICC Division of Judicial Services Marc Dubuisson told Korner that "everything is on track" regarding the preparations for AVL witnesses.
Dubuisson suggested that the schedule for AVL witnesses be started earlier, citing the seven-hour time difference.
"If we do it [this suggestion], we have to finish at 8:00 p.m. in the Philippines -- if the hearing ends at 1:00 p.m. in The Hague, that won't fit the schedule," Dubuisson told Korner.
For the defense, Haynes told the chamber of the logistical challenges of starting hearings at 8 a.m. in The Hague, including the need to transport Duterte to and from Scheveningen Prison.
Trial Chamber III has yet to release an order regarding the schedule for AVL witnesses.
Duterte is facing three counts of crimes against humanity involving murder and attempted murder allegedly committed during his terms as Davao City mayor and Philippine president.
His trial is scheduled to open on November 30 before Trial Chamber III, composed of Korner and Judges Keebong Paek and Nicolas Guillou. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Should AI companies pay for the journalism they use?
articles.summary: Publishers say AI chatbots are using their reporting to answer readers' questions while sending back less traffic and less money. Should the companies that build these tools pay for the journalism…

image.caption: Microsoft, Anthropic and OpenAI have said they support clearer signals that let website owners say if their content may be used to train AI modelsImage: Matteo Della Torre/NurPhoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: Millions of people now use AI chatbots as a source of news to find quick answers to questions about current events.

A 2026 survey by the Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, which questioned more than 90,000 people worldwide, found that 10% use AI chatbots for news on a weekly basis, a figure that is significantly higher among younger audiences.

Explaining what is happening in the world, why it matters and what it means has traditionally been the work of journalism. Media organizations send reporters into the field, commission investigations and conduct research, producing stories that help audiences understand global events. But as more people turn to AI tools for information, the relationship between those producing journalism and those distributing it is changing.

"In the past, search engines like Google indexed our websites and directed users to their articles, generating traffic in return," Julia Becker, publisher of Funke Media Group, told a panel at the Global Media Forum (GMF) in Berlin on November 5. "But now that exchange has broken down."

blocks.caption: Publishers, legal experts and tech companies debated who should pay for journalism used in AI systems at the Global Media Forum in BerlinImage: Stephanie Englert/DW Images

blocks.text: "AI companies draw on our quality reporting to generate answers, yet the reporting itself often remains largely invisible by the end of this process," said DW Director General Barbara Massing in a keynote address at the forum.

Their remarks reflect a worry that is growing across the media industry. Publicly available news is copied and summarized by AI chatbots, while news organizations are becoming less and less able to rely on the money and visibility that used to come from distributing that work.
Journalism and AI: A growing imbalance?

There has been growing concern about how copyrighted material is collected, used, and reproduced by artificial intelligence, and whether the companies that build those systems should pay the people and organizations that created the material.
Media houses are now pressing Big Tech companies to ask permission before using their work and to pay for it.

In October, German broadcasters ARD and RTL, along with the country's Federal Association of Digital Publishers and Newspaper Publishers (BDZV) and the Association of Private Media (VAUNET), called for stronger copyright protections for media companies.
In the US, lawsuits are adding pressure. The New York Times has sued internet company Brave Softwarefor allegedly using its content without permission and getting around its paywall.
Is the internet dying?
Meanwhile, legal institutions in the EU, including the European Court of Justice are examining whether AI-generated answers can themselves infringe copyright.

In February, a coalition of media organizations, including The Guardian, the BBC and the Financial Times called for rules that would give publishers more control over how AI systems copy and reproduce their content.
The problem goes beyond whether AI companies may use journalism. It also concerns how publishers and journalists can get paid when their work becomes part of the answers AI systems generate.
"AI systems shouldn't just use quality journalism. They should also pay for it," said Massing.
How could AI companies pay for the content they use?

Martin Senftleben, a professor at the University of Amsterdam who directs the Institute for Information Law, separates two ways AI companies use journalistic material: training their models and generating responses to individual user questions.
Payment for training is a more complicated legal question, he said. The more urgent issue is what happens when an AI system uses journalism to answer a question in real time.

He argued that European copyright law may already offer a way to address part of the problem. Under existing EU law, publishers and journalists may be able to claim payment collectively, without waiting for a new legal framework.
"What are we waiting for? Germany is a large member state. This should be introduced in Germany," he told the forum in Berlin.
Digital clones, real money: how athletes are trying to cash in on AI

One option, Senftleben suggested, is a legally required payment system in which every AI response that draws on journalism triggers a payment. A collecting organization would gather the money and distribute it among publishers and journalists, in the same way that music royalties are collected and distributed.
Once such a system exists, publishers and authors could use its rates as a starting point when negotiating individual licensing deals with AI companies.
Existing deals and concerns about too much regulation

Lutz Mache, senior manager of government affairs and public policy at Google, told the GMF panel that Google is willing to negotiate agreements with German media companies and to discuss new AI products with them.

Google has also started testing other ways to pay publishers for their contributions to AI-generated answers. Its "AI Contribution" pilot, which is being tested with selected publishers, aims to reward content that plays a significant role in answers produced by products such as Gemini and AI Overviews. But the program is still an early experiment, not a general payment system open to all publishers.

blocks.caption: Google has said its ancillary copyright agreements cover more than 800 German publications with payments already being madeImage: Stephanie Englert/DW Images

blocks.text: Microsoft, Anthropic and OpenAI have recently said they support clearer, standardized signals that let website owners state whether their content may be used to train AI models.
However, not everyone thinks more regulation is the answer.

Joerg Heidrich, a lawyer who specializes in technology law and serves as AI commissioner at the German media company Heise, warned against adding new rules without considering their effects on the wider tech sector.
Europe has already fallen behind in the global AI race, he argued. More regulation, he warned, could make it harder for European companies to compete with major providers based elsewhere.

Heidrich also pointed to smaller players, including startups, independent developers and research institutions, who depend on access to data to build and train AI systems. He argued that the debate over copyright and payment risks overlooking these groups, and that new restrictions could hurt their work.

articles.title: Prosecution rejects claim of failure in Sara Duterte impeachment trial
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel rejected remarks from Vice President Sara Duterte"s spokesperson claiming that the prosecution had failed, with one lawmaker asking: “In what alternate universe did we…

blocks.text: The House prosecution panel rejected remarks from Vice President Sara Duterte’s spokesperson claiming that the prosecution had failed, with one lawmaker asking: “In what alternate universe did we fail?”
Duterte’s spokesperson, Atty. Salvador Paolo Panelo Jr., made the remarks about the impeachment trial, saying the prosecution had failed.
During a news forum on Saturday, House prosecutor and Bicol Saro party-list Representative Terry Ridon said Panelo must have woken up in a bad mood.

“In what alternate universe did we actually fail at this point? Kasi ang totoo naman, if we failed, hindi pasok yung mga ebidensya na ito. Hindi sila maco-compel na sagutin po yung usapin, point per point in this defense presentation of evidence,” Ridon said.

(In what alternate universe did we actually fail at this point? The truth is, if we had failed, this evidence would not have been admitted. They would not have been compelled to address the issues point by point in this presentation of evidence by the defense.)

“So hindi ko alam kung masama lang yung gising ni Attorney Panelo pero hindi ko alam kung saang universo hinugot itong pagtingin po niya sa aktwal na estado ng paglilitis po niya ngayon,” Ridon added.
(So I do not know if Atty. Panelo simply woke up in a bad mood, but I do not know which universe he is getting this assessment of the actual state of the trial from.)

Meanwhile, House prosecution spokesperson Jay Tolosa said that declaring the prosecution unsuccessful would mean that its efforts had been futile. However, he pointed out that the defense had already lined up several witnesses.
“Sa first week pa lang, they already want to present 24 witnesses. So parang hindi masyadong consistent ito,” Tolosa said.
(In just the first week, they already want to present 24 witnesses. So that does not seem very consistent.)

Asked about surveys showing that Duterte’s defense panel had earned more favorable public opinion, Ridon said the prosecution was not dismissing the polls but stressed that the impeachment trial was not a popularity contest.

“Hindi naman ito Miss Universe. Hindi po ito beauty contest. Hindi po ito pasikatan. Hindi po ito popularity contest. Gagawin ng prosekusyon ang kailangan niyang gawin para patunayan yung ebidensya, para patunayan ang paratang laban sa Pangalawang Pangulo,” Ridon said.

(This is not Miss Universe. This is not a beauty contest. This is not about gaining fame or popularity. The prosecution will do what it needs to do to establish the evidence and prove the allegations against the Vice President.)
Ridon also said the survey results showed signs of partisanship, citing differences in the results across the regions where the poll was conducted.
Tolosa, for his part, described the particular survey as “stale,” noting that it was conducted before the article on unexplained wealth was presented.
Ready for Duterte
Tolosa said the prosecution was prepared for whatever the defense had planned, including the possibility of Duterte herself taking the witness stand.
“Kahit sino yung ma-presenta nila na witnesses, we will welcome it, even if they will finally call to the stand, the Vice President herself, we will of course, welcome that,” Tolosa said.
Tolosa added that several surveys indicated that the public wanted Duterte herself to explain the allegations against her.

With many of the defense witnesses reportedly consisting of staff members, Tolosa was asked whether they could simply claim that errors had been made in filing financial records and that Duterte had nothing to do with them.
Tolosa explained that many of the allegations stemmed from the Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN), a document that Duterte herself had signed.
“We all know, the Vice President, of course, is also a lawyer. So, alam niya kung ano yung significance, kapag pinirmahan niya yung isa dokumento and much more kapag notariado,” Tolosa said.
(We all know that the Vice President is also a lawyer. So she understands the significance of signing a document, especially when it is notarized.)
Discussing dropped articles could cause delays
In a report by Vonne Aquino on “24 Oras Weekend,” the prosecution team said the defense should no longer be allowed to present evidence on Articles I, III, and IV, which had already been withdrawn.
“Sana ma-address na head on itong issues sa unexplained wealth para ma-wrap up na rin natin itong unexplained wealth, the sole remaining article. Hopefully, [by] the end of the year,” Tolosa said.
(I hope the issues surrounding unexplained wealth, the sole remaining article, can be addressed head-on so we can wrap up the proceedings. Hopefully, by the end of the year.)

“Kung mag pe-presenta pa sila ng ebidensya para doon, it will not serve any legitimate purpose kasi nga, at the end of the trial, ang pagbobotohan nalang dito, kung dapat ma-convict o hindi ang bise presidente, yung unexplained wealth nalang,” Tolosa said.

(If they still present evidence on those articles, it will serve no legitimate purpose because, at the end of the trial, the only issue to be voted on is whether the Vice President should be convicted based on the remaining article on unexplained wealth.)
The defense had been given 30 days to answer the four articles of impeachment. Tolosa said it would only be reasonable to shorten the period following the withdrawal of three of the charges.
“Dapat ma-set po yan, kung ilang days na lang talaga yung binigay sa kanila so that they will not be allowed to drag this indefinitely,” Tolosa said.
(That should be set in terms of how many days they will actually be given, so they will not be allowed to drag this out indefinitely.)
The impeachment trial will resume on Monday, November 9, at 10 a.m. —VBL, GMA News
